page: Microsoft Azure D64nls_v6 is a network-optimized, low-memory virtual machine belonging to the Dnlv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, including AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21,489.0 and a top-tier image processing score of 20,362.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks are strong, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4,126.81 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 107.65 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 349.14 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations performed at 72.31 million operations per second. For LLM inference workloads, the processor processed 258.63 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B model.

The primary tradeoff of the D64nls_v6 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU and the complete absence of local storage, which requires relying on external premium storage. However, the high-frequency Intel Xeon processor and AMX instruction support provide high compute density, making it cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. This server is suitable for compute-intensive tasks, network-optimized applications, software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference prompt processing.
